title: Producing Alcohols
page_title: Producing Alcohols | Cambridge (CIE) AS Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- **Alcohols **are compounds that contain at least one **hydroxy **(-OH) group
- The general formula of alcohols is **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n+1**</sub>**OH**
- Alcohols can be prepared by a wide range of chemical reactions

- When hot steam is reacted with an alkene, using concentrated phosphoric(V) acid (**H**<sub>**3**</sub>**PO**<sub>**4**</sub>**) **as a catalyst, ***electrophilic addition*** takes place to form an **alcohol**

blocks.text: The electrophilic addition of ethene using water

blocks.alt: Chemical reaction showing ethene and steam forming ethanol, with H₃PO₄ and heat as catalysts. Ethene and ethanol molecular structures depicted.
blocks.caption: Electrophilic addition of steam to alkenes forms alcohols

blocks.md:
- Cold, dilute KMnO<sub>4</sub> is a **mild oxidising agent** and oxidises **alkenes**
- The C-C double bond is not fully broken and a diol is formed

  - A diol is a compound with two hydroxy, -OH, groups

blocks.text: Oxidation of ethene using cold, dilute KMnO<sub>4</sub>

blocks.alt: Hydroxy Compounds Oxidation, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes
blocks.caption: The oxidation of alkenes using cold, dilute KMnO4 forms a diol

blocks.md: - The halide atom in halogenoalkanes can be substituted when heated with aqueous NaOH in a ***nucleophilic substitution*** reaction

blocks.text: Nucleophilic substitution of bromoethane using NaOH

blocks.alt: Ethene reacts with water and an oxidising agent, [O], to form ethane-1,2-diol (reaction with cold dilute KMnO4)
blocks.caption: The nucleophilic substitution of halogenoalkanes using NaOH forms an alcohol

blocks.md: - **Aldehydes **and **ketones **can be reduced by reducing agents such as NaBH<sub>4</sub> or LiAlH<sub>4</sub>

- Aldehydes are reduced to **primary alcohols**

  - The carbon attached to the hydroxy group is bonded to one other alkyl group
- Ketones are reduced to **secondary alcohols**

  - The carbon attached to the hydroxy group is bonded to two other alkyl groups

blocks.text: The reduction of ethanal and propanone

blocks.alt: Chemical equations showing ethanal to ethanol and propanone to propan-2-ol, both with hydrogen addition. Ethanol is a primary alcohol, propan-2-ol secondary.
blocks.caption: The reduction of aldehydes and ketones forms primary and secondary alcohols respectively

blocks.md:
- Similarly, carboxylic acids are reduced by LiAlH<sub>4</sub> to primary alcohols
- NaBH<sub>4</sub> is not used as it is not a strong enough reducing agent for this reaction

blocks.alt: Ethanoic acid is reduced by 4[H] (from LiAlH4) to ethanol and water
blocks.caption: The reduction of carboxylic acids forms primary alcohols

blocks.md:
- Esters are made by a **condensation reaction** between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid
- When an ester is heated with dilute acid or alkali, **hydrolysis** will take place and the carboxylic acid and alcohol will be reformed

blocks.text: Acidic and alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate

blocks.alt: Chemical reactions of ethyl ethanoate: hydrolysis forming ethanoic acid and ethanol, and saponification forming sodium ethanoate and ethanol.
blocks.caption: The hydrolysis of esters forms alcohols
